text: Rome. The emperor Vespasian has a problem. The treasury is empty.
My guess was a fine for peeing in the street. Wrong!
Pee was useful. Laundries washed wool with it.
So Vespasian put a tax on it.
The emperor held a coin under his nose. Does it smell?
No. Yet it comes from pee.
That is why Rome taxed pee. The money did not smell.
In Paris, street urinals were later named after him. Vespasiennes.
